questions.q: What problem does a DMZ exist to solve?
options: Limiting the damage if a public-facing server, which is realistically the most likely host to be breached, is compromised
Making public-facing servers completely immune to compromise
Eliminating the need for any firewall between the internet and internal network
Speeding up internet traffic for employee workstations
questions.explain: The DMZ doesn't prevent a breach of a public server — it limits what that breach can reach next.

questions.q: Why is a public-facing web server placed in a DMZ rather than directly on the internal network?
options: So a breach of the web server lands the attacker in the DMZ, not on the internal network with finance servers and workstations
Because DMZ servers run faster than internal network servers
Because the internal network cannot physically connect to the internet
Because web servers require a different operating system than internal servers
questions.explain: The DMZ isolates public-facing hosts so a compromise there doesn't directly hand an attacker the internal network.

options: One firewall with three interfaces — internet, DMZ, and internal — each with its own rule set
Three separate DMZ segments connected in a loop
A DMZ with no firewall at all
Three firewalls, one for each department
questions.explain: A three-legged DMZ uses a single firewall device with three distinct interfaces, one per zone.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff of a back-to-back DMZ compared to a three-legged DMZ?
options: More hardware to buy and maintain, in exchange for requiring two independent firewall hops before reaching the internal network
It requires no firewall at all, which is less secure
It is always cheaper to deploy than a three-legged DMZ
It eliminates the need for a DMZ entirely
questions.explain: Back-to-back DMZs add defense in depth via two independent firewalls, at the cost of more hardware to manage.

questions.q: If a DMZ web server is compromised, what does an attacker still have to do to reach the internal network?
options: Get past another firewall boundary separating the DMZ from the internal network
Nothing — the internal network is immediately exposed
Wait for the internal network's IP address to change
Physically access the internal network's server room
questions.explain: The DMZ is designed so a breach there still requires clearing another firewall boundary to reach the internal network.
